content: Health 21 is the title assigned to the 1999 WHO European Region document, Health 21 Health for All in the 21st Century. This document was named as such because it not only addressed health challenges and goals for the 21st century but also outlined 21 specific principles and objectives aimed at improving the health of populations across Europe. The central theme of Health 21 is the promotion of equality in health, with a particular focus on reducing health inequalities. The document also identifies specific target groups for health promotion efforts. These groups include children, older adults, individuals at risk of or affected by communicable and infectious diseases, and those who misuse substances such as tobacco, drugs, or alcohol.
